title: An affine product chart covers the neutral part of a Néron lft-group
statement:
Let $D$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one, $K=\operatorname{Frac}D$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $V/K$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite type, and let $N/S$ be a Néron lft-model of $V$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus $N$ is a smooth separated commutative $S$-group scheme, with a specified generic-fibre group isomorphism $N_K\simeq V$ [def-pc-base-change], such that restriction is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(Y,N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_K(Y_K,V)$ for every smooth $S$-scheme $Y$. A group scheme has multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms satisfying the group diagrams [def-sc-group-scheme]; separated means the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $C\subseteq |N|$ be the union of the identity connected components of all geometric fibres, viewed as a subset of $|N|$ [def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Then $C$ is open, and its open subscheme structure makes it a subgroup scheme $N^0\subseteq N$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every $s\in S$ there is an affine open neighbourhood $B\subseteq S$ of $s$ and an affine open subscheme $U\subseteq N^0\times_SB$ such that the restriction of multiplication
$$U\times_BU\longrightarrow N^0\times_SB$$
is surjective on underlying points [def-pc-fibre-product]. In particular the image is the entire indicated open subgroup; no finiteness of the component groups of $N$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $f:N\to S$ and $e:S\to N$. By [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian], the ordinary fibrewise component locus through $e$ pulls back to the corresponding locus under every base change. On $N_{\bar s}$ it is $(N_{\bar s})^0$, so it is exactly the subset $C$ of the item. The theorem [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] applies to $N_{\bar s}$: its base-change smoothness, hence local finite type, follows affine-locally from the two cited smooth-ring lemmas. It shows $(N_{\bar s})^0$ is geometrically irreducible and of finite type, hence quasi-compact. The projection $N_{\bar s}\to N_s$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], applied to the surjection $\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(s)}\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. The component base-change equality shows that the image of $(N_{\bar s})^0$ is precisely $C_s$. Thus $C_s$ is connected and quasi-compact by continuity and [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact].

Fix $x\in C_s$. The image $e(S)$ is quasi-compact since $S$ is affine. Together with the quasi-compact $C_s$ it is contained in a finite union $W$ of affine opens of $N$. The restricted map $W\to S$ is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], applied to the open immersion $W\hookrightarrow N$, and $e$ factors through $W$. It is quasi-compact: on each affine chart, preimages of principal base opens are principal affine, and every affine base open has a finite cover by principal opens. It is quasi-separated: intersections of these affine charts are inverse images of the closed diagonal of $N/S$ in their affine fibre product, hence affine by the affine description of a closed immersion. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-section-component-open] to $W\to S$ and its section, obtaining an open $W^0$. The whole connected set $C_s$ lies in $W_s$, so its component through $e(s)$ is precisely $C_s$ and $x\in W^0$. On every fibre the component through $e(t)$ in $W_t$ maps into the component through $e(t)$ in $N_t$, so $W^0\subset C$. Every $x\in C$ thus has an open neighbourhood in $N$ contained in $C$. Hence $C$ is open.

source.place: Tag 055R, lemma-connected-along-section-open, applied only to quasi-compact open pieces containing the section; extension to N by open neighbourhoods.

proof.text: Give $C$ its open subscheme structure. On each geometric fibre it is the open subgroup $(N_{\bar s})^0$ by step 1 and [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component]. Multiplication $C\times_SC\to N$ and inversion $C\to N$ therefore have image in $C$: lift any source point to an algebraically closed extension $\Omega$ of its residue field, note that by [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian] for the base change along $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ the inverse image of $C$ in $N_\Omega$ is $(N_\Omega)^0$, apply the subgroup assertion there, and project back. The identity also has image in $C$. The factorization lemma [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] gives the three maps into $C$. Each group identity holds after composing with $C\hookrightarrow N$ because it holds in $N$; uniqueness of factorization through the open subscheme makes its two sides equal. Thus $N^0=C$ is the required open subgroup.

source.place: Tag 0B7R, proposition-connected-component, subgroup operations; BLR 6.4 discussion preceding Lemma 3.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and choose an affine open $A\subset N^0$ containing $e(s)$. Its structure map is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], so [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion] gives flatness and local finite presentation. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], $f(A)$ is an open neighbourhood of $s$. Choose a principal base open $B=D(a)$ with $s\in B\subset f(A)$. Put $U=A\times_SB$, an open in $N^0\times_SB$. It is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Every $U_t$ for $t\in B$ is nonempty. After any algebraically closed extension $\Omega/\kappa(t)$ it remains nonempty: [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] makes $U_t\times_{\kappa(t)}\Omega\to U_t$ surjective. By [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian] for the base change along $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, $(N^0)_\Omega=(N_\Omega)^0$, which is irreducible by [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component], and $U_\Omega$ is a nonempty open, hence dense. This constructs a fibrewise dense affine chart without assuming $N$ quasi-compact.

source.place: 10.1 paragraph after Definition 1, printed p.290/PDF p.296; affine chart simplified using geometrically irreducible neutral fibres; Stacks Tags 01V8, 01VF and 01UA for the open image.

proof.text: Let $x\in N^0\times_SB$ lie over $t$, choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(x)$, and let $g:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to(N^0)_t$ be its point above $x$. In the irreducible $\Omega$-group $G=(N^0)_\Omega$ (step 4), using its group law [def-sc-group-scheme] on points, both $U_\Omega$ and $gU_\Omega^{-1}$ are nonempty opens: the latter is its image under the isomorphism $h\mapsto gh^{-1}$ with inverse $h\mapsto h^{-1}g$. Irreducibility gives a point $z$ in their intersection. Put $L=\kappa(z)$. Its induced $L$-point $u$ lies in $U_L$, and $v=u^{-1}g_L$ also lies in $U_L$ because $u\in g_LU_L^{-1}$. Then $uv=g_L$. The fibre-product universal property gives $(u,v):\operatorname{Spec}L\to U\times_BU$ whose multiplication image is $g_L$, hence whose underlying point maps to $x$. Thus multiplication $U\times_BU\to N^0\times_SB$ is surjective on underlying points.

The statement (identity components of the geometric fibres form an open subgroup N^0; locally on S an affine U ⊂ N^0_B with U×_B U → N^0_B surjective) holds for any smooth separated S-group, so it holds here. It is unchanged from base and checked on small cases: trivial group, zero-dimensional and imperfect fibres, a split torus's lft-model. Sources: BLR is not in literature/; the worker records WANTED and proof_origin agent, which is right. I read Stacks 0B7R (groupoids proposition-connected-component) and 055R (more-morphisms lemma-connected-along-section-open); 055R needs finite presentation, matching the qcqs hypothesis that step 2 correctly establishes. Steps: step 1 is correct (component-cartesian lemma, field identity-component lemma, surjective base change). Step 2 is correct: a finite affine union W containing e(S) and C_s is qc, and qs via the closed diagonal, an affine fibre product and the affine description of a closed immersion. Step 3 factors the group maps through the open subscheme. Step 4 uses smooth ⇒ flat and lfp ⇒ open map to get B = D(a) and an affine, fibrewise dense U. Step 5 is a correct and complete g·U^{-1} ∩ U argument. FIX, C1 (missing citations): steps 2 and 4 justified the smoothness of an open piece inline although the Mathlib leaf lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition exists, so I cite it. Steps 3 and 4 used (N^0)_Ω = (N_Ω)^0 for an arbitrary algebraically closed Ω only 'by step 1', so I now cite lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian and, for irreducibility, the field lemma. Step 5 now cites def-sc-group-scheme. proof_deps is the union of the uses. Duplicates: lem-sfb-neron-neutral-local-properties (Q122) overlaps only partly (it assumes a geometrically connected H and has no product chart), so it is not a duplicate. lean.statement: theorem neronLft_neutralAffineProductChart (D K : Type u) [CommRing D] [IsDomain D] [IsNoetherianRing D] [IsIntegrallyClosed D] [Field K] [Algebra D K] [IsFractionRing D K] (_hDim : ringKrullDim D = 1) (V : Grp (Over (Spec (.of K)))) [IsCommMonObj V.X] [Smooth V.X.hom] [IsSeparated V.X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType V.X.hom] [QuasiCompact V.X.hom] (N : Grp (Over (Spec (.of D)))) [IsCommMonObj N.X] [Smooth N.X.hom] [IsSeparated N.X.hom] (α : (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap D K)))).mapGrp.obj N ≅ V) (_hNeron : ∀ (Y : Over (Spec (.of D))) [Smooth Y.hom], Function.Bijective (fun h : Y ⟶ N.X ↦ (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap D K)))).map h ≫ α.hom.hom.hom)) : ∃ C : N.X.left.Opens, (C : Set N.X.left) = {x | x ∈ connectedComponentIn (N.X.hom ⁻¹' {N.X.hom x}) (η[N.X].left (N.X.hom x))} ∧ ∃ (H : Grp (Over (Spec (.of D)))) (j : H ⟶ N), IsOpenImmersion j.hom.hom.left ∧ Set.range j.hom.hom.left = (C : Set N.X.left) ∧ ∀ s : Spec (.of D), ∃ B : (Spec (.of D)).Opens, s ∈ B ∧ IsAffine B.toScheme ∧ ∃ U : ((Over.pullback B.ι).mapGrp.obj H).X.left.Opens, IsAffine U.toScheme ∧ Surjective (groupOpenProductMap ((Over.pullback B.ι).mapGrp.obj H) U)
